key_insight: The paper shows that the choice of geometric invariant fundamentally changes stochastic vortex dynamics: SALT preserves circulation but is much more sensitive to high-wavenumber structure, while SFLT preserves energy and produces smoother, more diffuse uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: For turbulence modeling and uncertainty quantification, this means practitioners must choose between structure-preserving, gradient-sensitive perturbations and energy-preserving, globally smoother forcing depending on the flow features they want to represent.
method: Compare two stochastic 2D Euler frameworks: SALT (circulation-preserving) and SFLT (energy-preserving).
Analyze scale sensitivity, showing SALT noise effects grow like |k|^2 relative to SFLT.
Test both approaches on a traveling dipole, vortex merger, and forced-damped turbulence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments across three benchmark flows, and the results consistently show SALT uncertainty concentrated near sharp vorticity gradients while SFLT spreads variance more broadly across the domain.
watch_item: Preserving both circulation and energy simultaneously is not generally possible except through a stochastic reparametrization of time, so model choice involves an inherent trade-off.
paper_title: Numerical comparison of energy- versus circulation-preserving stochastic vortex dynamics
